title: Machine learning-designed TADF molecules synthesized and characterized
summary: Two molecules chosen from 19 screened ML-designed thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) candidates were synthesized by palladium-catalyzed coupling and showed delayed fluorescence; photoluminescence quantum yield was 9.9% (mol_12, chloroform) and 19.8% (mol_16, toluene), with a singlet-triplet gap of 0.0084 eV for mol_12. Structures were confirmed by NMR and photophysics by steady-state and transient PL, supported by quantum-chemical calculations. The ML design model comes from the authors' earlier work; quantum yields are modest, measurements are in solution only, and only two molecules were made.
ai_technology: Adversarial-generation and fine-screening ML models (from the authors' prior work) designed the TADF candidate database
organization: Chengdu Polytechnic; Sichuan Provincial Engineering Research Center of Thermoelectric Materials and Devices

evidence.tested: Two ML-designed TADF molecules were synthesized and measured by NMR, steady-state and transient photoluminescence, with quantum-chemical calculations.
evidence.unknown: Device performance, solid-state behavior and the generality of the ML design approach were not shown in the reviewed text.
evidence.ai_role: Generated and screened candidate TADF molecules; two of 19 were selected for synthesis.
